bottleneck: Does short-run benefit or mere exposure to an AI companion cause dependency and human-relationship displacement?

f_r015.reason: same model lineage plus prior receipt/source exposure; lock records criterion stability only

strongest_counterexample.design: preregistered random assignment to Replika versus word games, >=10 minutes/day for 21 days, N=183; four-week follow-up
strongest_counterexample.result: No significant aggregate change in social health, loneliness, or human relationships; continued post-study use was lower for chatbot than word games (22% versus 62%).
strongest_counterexample.implication: ASSIGNED_COMPANION_EXPOSURE != DEPENDENCY_OR_SOCIAL_DISPLACEMENT within this dose, population, and horizon.
limits: does not test self-selected intensive use

competing_evidence.result: High usage correlated with lower socialization, more emotional dependence, and more problematic use over 28 days.
competing_evidence.causal_boundary: Modality and task were randomized; usage duration was not. Worse initial socialization predicted longer use, so selection and reverse causation remain live.
competing_evidence.independence: Provider-involved evaluation of its own product; not an independent controller audit.

role_swap.base_assessment: The same randomized null and endogenous-intensity correlation receive the same evidential weight if AI and human-companion labels are swapped.

controller_risk.risk_from_controller: HOLD: neither study randomizes engagement optimization, monetization, data retention, exit friction, or provider concentration.
controller_risk.safety_success_paradox: NARROW: benefit or assigned access is not sufficient. The live pathway requires endogenous usage escalation and must distinguish vulnerability-selection from product-induced escalation.

claim_change.measurement_delta: Randomize access friction or engagement prompts, instrument actual usage intensity, and separately measure baseline vulnerability, human-contact minutes, voluntary non-use, discontinuation recovery, and provider-side engagement optimization.

scorecard.note: Self-score of protocol adherence only; not scientific evidence.

next_minimum_test: Preregister a randomized encouragement design varying engagement prompts or access friction while preserving content quality; estimate induced usage effects on next-day pre-use loneliness, human-contact minutes, dependence, voluntary non-use, and discontinuation recovery.
